title: Colliders & Rigidbody Basics
description: Add physical boundaries with colliders and bring your objects to life with Rigidbody physics.

slides.title: Colliders – Invisible Boundaries 🧱
slides.content:
# Defining Physical Shapes

A **Collider** is a component that defines the shape of an object for **physics** purposes. It doesn't need to match the visual mesh exactly.

Common collider types:
- **Box Collider** – for cubes, walls.
- **Sphere Collider** – for balls, planets.
- **Capsule Collider** – for characters.
- **Mesh Collider** – uses the actual mesh geometry (heavy, use sparingly).

Colliders can be marked as **trigger** (Is Trigger) to detect overlap without physical collision.

quizData.question: What does a Collider do?

options.text: It defines the physical shape for collision detection

quizData.explanation: Colliders provide the boundaries used by the physics engine to detect collisions.

slides.title: Rigidbody – The Physics Engine 🏋️
slides.content:
# Adding Mass and Forces

A **Rigidbody** component gives a GameObject mass, gravity, and the ability to respond to forces.

- **Mass** – affects how forces move it (heavier objects need more force).
- **Drag** – air resistance (slows linear movement).
- **Angular Drag** – slows rotation.
- **Use Gravity** – if checked, the object falls downwards.
- **Is Kinematic** – if true, the object ignores physics forces but can still move via script/transform (useful for moving platforms).

Without a Rigidbody, colliders will not react physically (they only detect static collisions).

quizData.question: What happens if you have a Collider but no Rigidbody?

options.text: The object falls through the ground
The object can detect collisions but doesn't react with physics motion

quizData.explanation: Colliders without Rigidbody are considered static; they can be collided with, but they don't move under physics.

slides.title: Is Trigger & Collision Events 🔔
slides.content:
# Detecting Overlaps

- **Is Trigger** (on collider): The object doesn't physically block, but triggers events when something enters its area.
- **OnCollisionEnter** – called when two non‑trigger colliders hit.
- **OnTriggerEnter** – called when a collider enters a trigger zone.

These events are scripted in C# and will be covered later in scripting lessons. For now, remember that triggers are essential for pickups, checkpoints, and sensor zones.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Optimize Colliders

Use primitive colliders (Box, Sphere, Capsule) instead of Mesh Colliders whenever possible. Mesh Colliders are expensive. For complex shapes, combine multiple primitives.
